original.target_description: Study 1, second randomized condition: matching inauguration photographs to presidents, Trump versus Clinton voter comparison discussed on p. 141 and illustrated by education in Figure 4. Vote choice is the original operationalization; no Republican-versus-Democrat test is reported.

n.quote:
The other half of respondents received the same set of photographs, but
               were asked which photo was from Trump’s inauguration and which was
               from Obama’s. ... Figure 4. Percent Making an Incorrect Match of the Inauguration
                Photograph to the President by 2016 Vote Choice, Trump Approval, and
                Education. Figure shows percent choosing image A as belonging to Obama’s
                inauguration and image B as belonging to Trump’s with sampling weights
                employed. High-education respondents are those with at least a college de-
                gree, and low-education respondents are those with some college or less.
n.sample_role: Analytic respondents in the second-condition Trump-versus-Clinton photograph-identification comparison; count not explicitly printed.
n.exclusions: Third-party voters excluded generally; no second-condition final voter-group counts or additional exclusions printed.

notes: Source describes about 40 percent of Trump voters, about 20 percent of nonvoters and less than 10 percent of Clinton voters misidentifying the inauguration photographs. It gives no OR, numerical comparative effect/test statistic or p-value for that partisan identification comparison. Figure 4 displays education-specific descriptive percentages; these are not a scalar pooled partisan effect. The preceding p = .025 concerns education among strong Trump approvers in the first condition and cannot be assigned to this test. The Figure 2 N groups belong to the other randomized condition and cannot be reused. Whole-survey recruitment/completion counts and approximate half-sample allocation do not establish this analytic N. Only assigned unfinished original fields were examined for output; other fields and replication/success are unassigned placeholders.
